title: When Volcanoes Dim the Sun
question: How can a volcanic eruption cool the planet for years?
hook: Some of the coldest years of the last five thousand were caused by gas shot out of volcanoes.
idea: Sulfur gas lifted into the stratosphere becomes a reflective acid haze that cools the surface for years, and ice and ocean feedbacks can stretch the chill much longer.

beats.prompt: Put the steps from eruption to cooling in order.
items: SO₂ is injected into the stratosphere
It forms sulfuric acid aerosols within about a week
The aerosols circle the hemisphere within weeks
Their radiative effect cools the surface for several years
beats.explain: The gas first has to react into aerosols, which then spread around the hemisphere and keep reflecting sunlight for years.

beats.prompt: The same high-latitude volcano could erupt in winter or in summer, sending up the same gas. Which eruption has the stronger cooling effect?

choices.label: The winter eruption
choices.feedback: Winter feels colder, but at high latitudes winter injections work much less well because polar regions then clear the aerosols faster.

choices.label: No difference; only the amount of gas matters
choices.feedback: The season of an eruption is one of the factors that shape its climate impact.

beats.explain: For high-latitude eruptions, winter injections are much less radiatively efficient, because removal of stratospheric aerosols in polar regions is stronger then.

beats.prompt: Sort each into how long it lasts.
items: Acid droplets formed in the troposphere
beats.explain: Ash falls out in weeks and rain washes low droplets away in days, while stratospheric aerosols stay up long enough to cool the surface for years.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: A bigger eruption throws out a larger volume of material
So a bigger eruption must release more SO₂
SO₂ in the stratosphere forms the cooling aerosols
So the biggest eruptions always bring the worst cooling
beats.explain: Eruption size does not correlate with the amount of SO₂ released, which is why eruption size does not predict how severe the cooling is.
